format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
    toc: true

    fig-height: 4
execute:

```{r}
#| label: setup
here::i_am("reports/qc_report.qmd")
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

dat  <- readRDS(here::here("data/processed/02_annotate.rds"))
keep <- !dat$sample$excluded
X    <- log2(dat$intensity[, keep])
smp  <- dat$sample[keep, ]

complete <- rowSums(is.na(X)) == 0

run_qc <- smp |>
  select(run, batch, site, group, age, sex) |>
  mutate(
    n_quantified    = colSums(!is.na(X)),
    frac_missing    = colMeans(is.na(X)),
    median_observed = apply(X, 2, median, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_complete = apply(X[complete, ], 2, median)
  )

# Categorical palette validated for colour-vision deficiency; batch is also
# encoded by shape and axis labels, so colour never carries identity alone
batch_cols <- setNames(c("#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#1baf7a"), levels(smp$batch))

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "top")
)
```

Runs excluded by the authors (`r sum(!keep)`) are not shown; `r ncol(X)` runs
and `r nrow(X)` protein groups remain. `r sum(complete)` protein groups are
quantified in every run.

## Run-level summary

```{r}
#| label: tbl-batch
#| tbl-cap: "Run-level metrics by MS batch (mean across runs)."
run_qc |>
  group_by(batch) |>
  summarise(
    runs                 = n(),
    sites                = paste(unique(site), collapse = ", "),
    `proteins quantified` = round(mean(n_quantified)),
    `% missing`          = round(100 * mean(frac_missing), 1),
    `median log2 (observed)` = round(mean(median_observed), 2),
    `median log2 (complete)` = round(mean(median_complete), 2)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Proteins quantified per run

```{r}
#| label: fig-nquant
#| fig-cap: "Protein groups quantified per run, by MS batch."
ggplot(run_qc, aes(batch, n_quantified, colour = batch, shape = batch)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.5, colour = "grey55") +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 2.2, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = batch_cols) +
  labs(x = "MS batch", y = "Protein groups quantified") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## Missing values bias the median of observed intensities

Spectronaut's Local Normalization was applied across all runs. A per-run median
computed on observed values alone is inflated in runs with more missing values,
because missing values concentrate in low-abundance proteins.

```{r}
#| label: fig-median-vs-missing
#| fig-cap: "Per-run median log2 intensity of observed values against the fraction of missing values."
ggplot(run_qc, aes(frac_missing, median_observed, colour = batch, shape = batch)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = batch_cols) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = "Missing values in run", y = "Median log2 intensity (observed)",
       colour = "MS batch", shape = "MS batch")
```

Correlation between missing fraction and median:
`r round(cor(run_qc$frac_missing, run_qc$median_observed), 2)` using observed
values, `r round(cor(run_qc$frac_missing, run_qc$median_complete), 2)` using
only the `r sum(complete)` complete protein groups.

## Batch offset after removing the missingness effect

```{r}
#| label: fig-median-batch
#| fig-cap: "Per-run median log2 intensity by MS batch, on all observed values and on complete protein groups only."
run_qc |>
  pivot_longer(c(median_observed, median_complete),
               names_to = "set", values_to = "median") |>
  mutate(set = factor(set,
                      levels = c("median_observed", "median_complete"),
                      labels = c("All observed values",
                                 paste0("Complete protein groups (n = ", sum(complete), ")")))) |>
  ggplot(aes(batch, median, colour = batch, shape = batch)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.5, colour = "grey55") +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ set, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = batch_cols) +
  labs(x = "MS batch", y = "Median log2 intensity") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## Normalization assessment

Per-run medians of complete protein groups were modelled on batch and
diagnosis. Batch offsets are modelled as a covariate in limma rather than
removed by renormalization, because run-level centering would also remove the
small diagnosis-associated shift shown below.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-median-model
#| tbl-cap: "Linear model of per-run median log2 intensity (complete protein groups) on batch and diagnosis."
coef_table <- function(fit) {
  ci <- confint(fit)
  data.frame(
    term     = rownames(ci),
    estimate = round(coef(fit), 3),
    ci_low   = round(ci[, 1], 3),
    ci_high  = round(ci[, 2], 3),
    p        = signif(summary(fit)$coefficients[, 4], 2),
    row.names = NULL
  )
}
coef_table(lm(median_complete ~ batch + group, data = run_qc)) |> knitr::kable()
```

## Drivers of missingness

```{r}
#| label: tbl-missing-model
#| tbl-cap: "Linear model of the fraction of missing values per run on batch, age and diagnosis."
coef_table(lm(frac_missing ~ batch + age + group, data = run_qc)) |> knitr::kable()
```

Missingness depends on diagnosis after adjusting for batch and age, so missing
values are not independent of the contrast of interest. This rules out both
left-censored imputation and analysis of observed values only, and motivates a
model of the missingness mechanism in the differential abundance step.

## Runs with low protein coverage

Runs more than 3 median absolute deviations below their batch median in protein
groups quantified. All are retained; sample-level quality weights are estimated
in the limma model.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-flagged
#| tbl-cap: "Runs with low protein coverage relative to their MS batch."
run_qc |>
  group_by(batch) |>
  filter(n_quantified < median(n_quantified) - 3 * mad(n_quantified)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  transmute(run = substring(run, pmax(1, nchar(run) - 29)), batch, site, group, age,
            n_quantified, `% missing` = round(100 * frac_missing, 1),
            median_complete = round(median_complete, 2)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Blood contamination

Erythrocyte contamination is scored with a panel of erythrocyte-specific
proteins (Geyer et al., 2019, *EMBO Mol Med*). Each protein is z-scored across
runs, and the run score is the mean z-score of the panel proteins it contains.

```{r}
#| label: ery-score
ery_panel <- c("HBA1", "HBB", "HBD", "CA1", "CA2", "CAT", "PRDX2", "BLVRB", "SLC4A1")
gene_list <- strsplit(dat$protein$PG.Genes, ";")
in_panel  <- vapply(gene_list, function(g) any(g %in% ery_panel), logical(1))

Z <- t(scale(t(X[in_panel, ])))
run_qc$ery_score <- colMeans(Z, na.rm = TRUE)
```

Panel proteins found: `r sum(in_panel)` of `r length(ery_panel)`.

```{r}
#| label: fig-ery
#| fig-cap: "Erythrocyte contamination score per run, by MS batch and diagnosis. Dashed line: flagging threshold (median + 3 MAD)."
ery_cut_plot <- median(run_qc$ery_score) + 3 * mad(run_qc$ery_score)
ggplot(run_qc, aes(batch, ery_score, colour = group, shape = group)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey75") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = ery_cut_plot, colour = "grey45", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15, dodge.width = 0.6),
             size = 2.2, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(control = "#2a78d6", AD = "#eb6834")) +
  labs(x = "MS batch", y = "Erythrocyte score (mean z)",
       colour = "Diagnosis", shape = "Diagnosis")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ery-model
#| tbl-cap: "Linear model of the erythrocyte contamination score on batch and diagnosis."
coef_table(lm(ery_score ~ batch + group, data = run_qc)) |> knitr::kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: ery-flag
ery_cut <- median(run_qc$ery_score) + 3 * mad(run_qc$ery_score)
run_qc$ery_flag <- run_qc$ery_score > ery_cut
```

Contamination does not differ between diagnostic groups, so it is not expected
to bias the AD vs. control comparison. `r sum(run_qc$ery_flag)` runs exceed the
contamination threshold (median + 3 MAD = `r round(ery_cut, 2)`): all are
retained in the main analysis and removed in a sensitivity analysis. Protein
groups strongly correlated with the score are flagged as contamination-prone
in the differential abundance results.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ery-top
#| tbl-cap: "Runs with the highest erythrocyte contamination score. Runs above the threshold are flagged."
run_qc |>
  arrange(desc(ery_score)) |>
  transmute(run = substring(run, pmax(1, nchar(run) - 29)), batch, site, group,
            ery_score = round(ery_score, 2), flagged = ery_flag) |>
  head(10) |>
  knitr::kable()
```
